result.title: Evaluating Near-Perfect Accuracy Claims in Machine-Learning-Based Leak Detection for Two-Phase Pipelines: A Condition-Blocked Audit
result.comment: 8 figures, 8 tables. Analysis code archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24218226
result.summary: Reliable leak detection in gas-liquid two-phase pipelines is important for process safety, yet machine-learning studies frequently report near-perfect performance using evaluation protocols that may not represent deployment to unseen operating conditions. This study audits a pressure-based leak-detection model using condition-blocked leave-one-condition-out validation, in which the classifier is tested on a flow condition excluded from training. Accuracy decreased from 93.3% under within-condition evaluation to 59.1% across fifteen unseen-condition tests. Ablation analysis showed that most of this difference arose from the data-splitting protocol, with a smaller contribution from encoding operating conditions as model inputs. Under condition-blocked evaluation, the false-alarm and missed-detection rates increased to 34.1% and 10.2%, respectively, demonstrating that near-perfect reported accuracy did not translate into reliable operation at unseen flow conditions. The reduction persisted across all evaluated classifiers, indicating that it was caused by the evaluation design rather than a particular model architecture. Grouped evaluation of an independent acoustic pipeline dataset produced a comparable reduction toward chance-level performance. These findings show that validation units must represent the conditions encountered during deployment. Condition-blocked evaluation and explicit reporting of operational error rates are therefore necessary before machine-learning leak detectors can support process-safety decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 审计基于压力的两相管道泄漏检测模型，改用「留一工况」分块验证后，准确率由同工况下的 93.3% 降至未见过工况的 59.1%，并通过消融将落差主要归因于数据划分协议、次要归因于把工况编码为模型输入。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「分块/分组验证＋拆分信息泄漏消融＋报告运行层错误率」的评测设计，可能可供核查 LVR 与 VLM 推理评测中因划分方式或条件泄漏而虚高的收益；但领域本身与视觉推理无直接联系，属远域借鉴线索。
